title: k-fold Chinese Remainder Theorem: ℤ/(n₁···nₖ)ℤ ≅ ∏ᵢ ℤ/nᵢℤ
description: The Chinese Remainder Theorem extends from two coprime moduli to any finite list of pairwise coprime moduli. For pairwise coprime n₁, ..., nₖ, the ring ℤ/(n₁···nₖ)ℤ is isomorphic to the product ∏ᵢ ℤ/nᵢℤ. This formalization constructs the k-fold isomorphism by induction using Mathlib's 2-fold ZMod.chineseRemainder, with the key lemma that pairwise coprimality implies coprimality with the product of remaining moduli. Includes explicit 3-fold and 4-fold specializations and k-fold Euler totient multiplicativity.

overview.historicalContext: The Chinese Remainder Theorem originates in Sunzi Suanjing (~3rd century CE), which posed: 'find a number giving remainders 2, 3, 2 when divided by 3, 5, 7.' The first general algorithm for arbitrary moduli was given by Qin Jiushao in his 1247 Shushu Jiuzhang (Mathematical Treatise in Nine Sections), predating European treatments by centuries. Euler stated the k-fold version for pairwise coprime moduli, and Gauss gave it systematic treatment in Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801, Articles 32-36). The modern ring-theoretic formulation as an isomorphism $\mathbb{Z}/(\prod n_i)\mathbb{Z} \cong \prod_i \mathbb{Z}/n_i\mathbb{Z}$ captures both existence and uniqueness of solutions plus the full multiplicative structure. This k-fold generalization is foundational in modern cryptography: RSA key generation relies on the CRT decomposition $\mathbb{Z}/pq\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ for efficient decryption, and multi-prime RSA uses the k-fold version directly.
overview.problemStatement:
**Theorem (crtKFold)**: For a list ns of pairwise coprime natural numbers,
  ZMod ns.prod ≃+* CRTProd ns
where CRTProd ns is the right-associated product ∏ᵢ ZMod (ns.get i).

**Key lemma (coprime_prod_of_coprime_all)**: If n is coprime to every element of ns, then n is coprime to ns.prod.
overview.text: A 249-line formalization of the $k$-fold Chinese Remainder Theorem as a ring isomorphism $\mathbb{Z}/(n_1 \cdots n_k)\mathbb{Z} \cong \prod_i \mathbb{Z}/n_i\mathbb{Z}$. Defines `CRTProd ns` as a right-associated product type and constructs `crtKFold` by induction on the modulus list, using the key lemma `coprime_prod_of_coprime_all` (pairwise coprimality implies $n$ is coprime to $\prod n_i$). Each inductive step composes Mathlib's 2-fold `ZMod.chineseRemainder` with the inductive hypothesis via `RingEquiv.prodCongr`. Base case: $\mathbb{Z}/1\mathbb{Z} \cong \text{PUnit}$. Includes explicit `crt3` and `crt4` specializations avoiding the `CRTProd` type, the $k$-fold Euler totient multiplicativity $\varphi(\prod n_i) = \prod \varphi(n_i)$, and cardinality preservation. Fully verified: 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Induction on the list of moduli**:

**Base**: Empty list — ZMod 1 ≅ PUnit (the trivial ring).

**Step**: Given n :: ns with pairwise coprimality:
1. By coprime_prod_of_coprime_all, n is coprime to ns.prod
2. Apply ZMod.chineseRemainder: ZMod (n * ns.prod) ≅ ZMod n × ZMod ns.prod
3. Apply IH: ZMod ns.prod ≅ CRTProd ns
4. Compose via RingEquiv.prodCongr

**Explicit specializations**: crt3 and crt4 construct 3-fold and 4-fold CRTs directly using associativity and mul_right, avoiding the CRTProd type.
keyInsights: The key enabling lemma is coprime_prod_of_coprime_all: pairwise coprimality propagates to products
CRTProd as a recursive type avoids the ZMod (n*1) ≠ ZMod n definitional equality issue
The base case ZMod 1 ≅ PUnit uses Subsingleton since ZMod 1 has exactly one element
Explicit crt3/crt4 use ring to prove associativity a*b*c = a*(b*c) at the ℕ level
All coprimality conditions are decidable, so examples use `by decide`

The k-fold totient multiplicativity φ(∏nᵢ) = ∏φ(nᵢ) is a 'free' corollary: the CRT isomorphism preserves units, so |(ℤ/∏nᵢℤ)*| = ∏|(ℤ/nᵢℤ)*| — the algebraic proof is more natural than the number-theoretic one

sections.title: Key Coprimality Lemma
sections.summary: coprime_prod_of_coprime_all and head_coprime_tail_prod: if n is coprime to each element, it's coprime to the product. Proved by induction using Nat.Coprime.mul_right. Also pairwise_tail: extracting pairwise coprimality of the tail from the cons case.
sections.mathContext: Key lemma: if $\gcd(n, n_i) = 1$ for all $i$, then $\gcd(n, \prod_i n_i) = 1$. Proved by induction: $\gcd(n, n_1 \cdot \prod_{i>1} n_i) = 1$ follows from $\gcd(n, n_1) = 1$ and $\gcd(n, \prod_{i>1} n_i) = 1$ via `Nat.Coprime.mul_right`. This is the essential ingredient enabling the inductive step of the $k$-fold CRT.

sections.title: Explicit 3-fold and 4-fold CRT
sections.summary: crt3 and crt4: direct constructions of ℤ/(abc)ℤ ≅ ℤ/aℤ × (ℤ/bℤ × ℤ/cℤ) and 4-fold analog. Uses ring for ℕ associativity, Nat.Coprime.mul_right for coprimality propagation, and RingEquiv.prodCongr for lifting isomorphisms into products.
sections.mathContext: Explicit 3-fold: $\mathbb{Z}/abc\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/a\mathbb{Z} \times (\mathbb{Z}/b\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})$ for pairwise coprime $a,b,c$. First apply `ZMod.chineseRemainder` to get $\mathbb{Z}/a(bc)\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/a\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/bc\mathbb{Z}$ (using $\gcd(a, bc) = 1$), then `RingEquiv.prodCongr` with the 2-fold CRT on $\mathbb{Z}/bc\mathbb{Z}$. The 4-fold version iterates the same pattern.

sections.title: General k-fold CRT Isomorphism
sections.summary: CRTProd recursive type definition, CommRing instances, zmod_one_equiv_punit base case, and crtKFold: the main inductive construction composing chineseRemainder with prodCongr at each step.
sections.mathContext: Define $\text{CRTProd}([]) = \text{PUnit}$, $\text{CRTProd}(n :: ns) = \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \times \text{CRTProd}(ns)$. The isomorphism $\mathbb{Z}/(\prod n_i)\mathbb{Z} \cong \text{CRTProd}(ns)$ is constructed by induction: at each step, $\mathbb{Z}/(n \cdot \prod ns)\mathbb{Z} \xrightarrow{\text{CRT}} \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/(\prod ns)\mathbb{Z} \xrightarrow{\text{id} \times \text{IH}} \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \times \text{CRTProd}(ns)$. Base case: $\mathbb{Z}/1\mathbb{Z} \cong \text{PUnit}$ since $\mathbb{Z}/1\mathbb{Z}$ is the trivial ring.

sections.title: Properties of the k-fold CRT
sections.summary: Algebraic properties derived from the ring isomorphism: bijective, injective, surjective, preserves multiplication and addition, round-trip identity in both directions. Each follows directly from RingEquiv API.
sections.mathContext: The ring isomorphism $\phi: \mathbb{Z}/(\prod n_i)\mathbb{Z} \xrightarrow{\sim} \text{CRTProd}(ns)$ satisfies: $\phi(x + y) = \phi(x) + \phi(y)$, $\phi(xy) = \phi(x)\phi(y)$ (ring homomorphism), $\phi^{-1} \circ \phi = \text{id}$ and $\phi \circ \phi^{-1} = \text{id}$ (bijectivity). All follow from the `RingEquiv` API since $\phi$ is constructed as a composition of `RingEquiv`s.

sections.title: Euler Totient Multiplicativity
sections.summary: totient_prod_pairwise_coprime: φ(∏ nᵢ) = ∏ φ(nᵢ) for pairwise coprime lists. Proved by induction using Nat.totient_mul at each step, mirroring the CRT induction structure.
sections.mathContext: Euler's totient $\varphi(n) = |\{k : 1 \leq k \leq n, \gcd(k,n) = 1\}|$ is multiplicative: $\varphi(mn) = \varphi(m)\varphi(n)$ when $\gcd(m,n)=1$. The $k$-fold version $\varphi(\prod_i n_i) = \prod_i \varphi(n_i)$ follows by induction, applying `Nat.totient_mul` at each step with coprimality $\gcd(n, \prod ns) = 1$ from `coprime_prod_of_coprime_all`.

sections.title: Concrete Examples
sections.summary: Concrete instances: ℤ/30ℤ ≅ ℤ/2ℤ × ℤ/3ℤ × ℤ/5ℤ (both via k-fold and explicit crt3), ℤ/210ℤ ≅ ℤ/2ℤ × ℤ/3ℤ × ℤ/5ℤ × ℤ/7ℤ (explicit crt4). Totient example: φ(30) = φ(2)·φ(3)·φ(5) = 8.
sections.mathContext: Example: $30 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$ with $\gcd(2,3) = \gcd(2,5) = \gcd(3,5) = 1$, so $\mathbb{Z}/30\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$. Totient: $\varphi(30) = \varphi(2) \cdot \varphi(3) \cdot \varphi(5) = 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 4 = 8$. The 4-fold example: $210 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 7$ gives $\varphi(210) = 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 4 \cdot 6 = 48$.

crossReferences.description: The root formalization: Bézout's identity ($\gcd(a,b) = ax + by$). The CRT builds on coprimality ($\gcd = 1$), which is the Bézout case yielding $1 = ax + by$.
Direct grandparent: explores the 2-fold CRT and its ring-theoretic formulation. This entry generalizes to arbitrary $k$-fold products.

The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (unique prime factorization) provides the canonical pairwise coprime decomposition $n = p_1^{a_1} \cdots p_k^{a_k}$, making the $k$-fold CRT applicable to any modulus.
The Euler totient function $\varphi(n)$. This file proves the $k$-fold multiplicativity $\varphi(\prod n_i) = \prod \varphi(n_i)$ as a CRT corollary, extending Euler's classical result.

Primitive roots modulo primes: $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^*$ is cyclic. The CRT decomposes $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^* \cong \prod (\mathbb{Z}/p_i^{a_i}\mathbb{Z})^*$, reducing unit group structure to prime power components.

Generalizes the CRT to non-coprime moduli: when $\gcd(m,n) > 1$, the system $x \equiv a \pmod{m}$, $x \equiv b \pmod{n}$ has a solution iff $a \equiv b \pmod{\gcd(m,n)}$. The coprime k-fold CRT here is the clean isomorphism case; the non-coprime version shows what happens when the coprimality hypothesis is dropped.

conclusion.summary: This formalization proves the k-fold Chinese Remainder Theorem with 0 axioms and 0 sorries: ZMod (∏ nᵢ) ≅ ∏ᵢ ZMod nᵢ for pairwise coprime nᵢ. The proof constructs the isomorphism by induction using Mathlib's 2-fold chineseRemainder, with explicit specializations for 3 and 4 moduli. The k-fold Euler totient multiplicativity follows as a corollary.
conclusion.implications:
**For number theory**: The k-fold CRT provides the foundation for prime factorization-based decompositions, Hensel lifting, and number-theoretic algorithms.

**For algebra**: Demonstrates the pattern of building k-ary constructions from binary ones using induction on lists.

**For Mathlib**: Could be contributed as a generalization of the existing ZMod.chineseRemainder.
openQuestions: Generalize to the ideal-theoretic CRT: R/∏Iᵢ ≅ ∏ R/Iᵢ for pairwise coprime ideals
Prove cardinality preservation: |ZMod (∏nᵢ)| = ∏|ZMod nᵢ| = ∏nᵢ for the k-fold case
Connect to the Pi-type formulation: ZMod (∏ nᵢ) ≅ (i : Fin k) → ZMod (ns i)
